# Working of the Program

#### Course: Learn Recursion With C++

## Working of the Program

![Each Recursive Call Returns ](data:image/png;base64,)

When the base condition is reached, the final function returns "Done".

This returned value then propagates back through the chain of recursive calls, ultimately leading to "Done" being returned to the original function call.

It's important to note that in each function call, we print the value of n before recursively calling the function. Thus, the numbers 1 and 2 are printed inside the function itself.

However, the string "Done" is returned by each recursive call (starting with the function call that satisfies the base condition) until this value is returned to the original function call.

The original function call then returns this value to the output variable, where "Done" is finally stored.

Next, we will modify this program so that each function call returns a different value.
